summary: Provides a mechanism for endpoints to request delivery, processing, and display notifications for page-mode instant messages. It extends the CPIM data format from RFC 3862 with new header fields and defines a message format for the notifications, plus how SIP entities behave. This is a Proposed Standard.

eli5.summary: When you send a chat message, you can ask for a note saying it arrived and was read. This defines how to ask for those notes and how they look.

questions: how do read receipts work in sip instant messaging
how do instant message read receipts work
what is the disposition-notification header in cpim
subtitle: Read receipts for page-mode instant messages: how a sender asks for, and a recipient returns, delivery, processing and display notifications.

tldr.problem: People who send instant messages often want to know whether the message arrived or was shown to the recipient. Email has a mechanism for this, but CPIM-based instant messaging did not.
tldr.mechanism: The sender adds CPIM header fields such as Disposition-Notification and Message-ID to the message. The recipient or an intermediary answers with an IMDN, a small XML document of type message/imdn+xml that reports a delivery, processing or display status.
tldr.outcome: Senders can get automatic receipts, but the RFC is clear that an IMDN is not proof that anyone read a message: it can be forged, lost, or silently withheld by a recipient who prefers privacy.

today: RFC 5438 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Instant Messages Need Receipts
sections.content:
Message senders often want to know whether the human recipient actually received a message or has it displayed. Email already answers this with Message Disposition Notifications (RFC 3798): after the recipient views a message, the mail client generates an MDN in a fixed format that software can process.

IMDN (Instant Message Disposition Notification) does the same for instant messages. It extends the CPIM message format of RFC 3862, which SIP can carry in MESSAGE requests (RFC 3428). The document covers page-mode messages only; session-mode is left for future work.
sections.eli5: Email can tell you when someone opened your letter. This RFC gives chat messages the same trick.

sections.title: Roles and Disposition Types
sections.content:
An IM Sender creates a message and requests notifications. An IM Recipient receives it and, if it chooses, sends back an IMDN. An intermediary is a network entity, most often an application server such as a URI-List or store-and-forward server, that forwards the message. A gateway is an intermediary that translates between different IM systems.

There are three categories of notification, called disposition types:

  • delivery: delivered, failed, forbidden or error.
  • processing: processed, stored, forbidden or error. Only intermediaries send these.
  • display: displayed, forbidden or error. The state displayed includes the start of rendering audio or video.

forbidden means the sender is denied the requested notification, for example because an administrator disallowed IMDNs. error means the fate of the message could not be determined. The RFC notes that without a positive acknowledgement from the user, nobody can tell whether the user actually read the message.
sections.eli5: There are three kinds of notes: "it got to the mailbox", "a helper in the middle handled it", and "it was put on the screen". None of them promise a person really read it.

sections.title: New CPIM Header Fields
sections.content:
IMDN adds header fields in a new CPIM namespace, urn:ietf:params:imdn, normally bound to the prefix imdn with an NS header. Clients may use any prefix, and servers and intermediaries must accept any legal one.

  • Disposition-Notification: which notifications the sender wants. Values are positive-delivery, negative-delivery, processing and display, separated by commas. An absent or empty field means no IMDNs are requested.
  • Message-ID: a globally unique identifier the sender uses to match IMDNs to messages. It is RECOMMENDED to come from a cryptographically secure random number generator and carry at least 64 bits of randomness, so off-path attackers cannot guess valid IDs and forge IMDNs.
  • Original-To: inserted by an intermediary that changes the CPIM To field, so the recipient can report the original address.
  • IMDN-Record-Route and IMDN-Route: let an intermediary stay on the return path of the IMDN.

A sender that wants IMDNs MUST include both Message-ID and a DateTime field. The timestamp is returned in the IMDN so that devices that cannot keep state, such as phones with limited memory, still let the user work out which message was meant.

The sender is not required to keep state or run timers. IMDNs may legitimately never arrive, and there is no time limit on when they may.
sections.eli5: You write a unique number on your letter and say which receipts you want. The receipt carries the same number so you can tell which letter it belongs to.

sections.title: How Recipients and Intermediaries Respond
sections.content:
The recipient looks at Disposition-Notification and may generate zero, one or several IMDNs, but it MUST NOT generate more than one IMDN per disposition type for the same message. Values it does not understand are ignored. A recipient MUST NOT generate processing notifications. It may also ignore the request entirely, as a per-message, per-sender or programmed policy choice.

An IMDN is itself a CPIM message with a fresh Message-ID and a Content-Disposition of notification. It must not request an IMDN of its own: nobody sends an IMDN for an IMDN. If the original message had IMDN-Record-Route fields, the recipient copies them, in order, into IMDN-Route fields and sends the IMDN to the top one. Otherwise it goes to the URI in the From field.

Intermediaries may insert Original-To (never overwriting an existing one) and IMDN-Record-Route. They are the only entities that build processing notifications, and they may build negative delivery notifications when an error was returned. A URI-List server may aggregate several IMDNs into one multipart/mixed message, waiting for a configurable period or until all recipients have answered. If list membership is not disclosed, it MUST remove the <recipient-uri> and <original-recipient-uri> elements before forwarding.
sections.eli5: The person getting your message decides whether to send a receipt, and sends at most one of each kind. Helpers in the middle can add their own notes, and a group-mailing helper can bundle many receipts into one envelope.

sections.title: The IMDN XML Payload
sections.content:
An IMDN payload is a well-formed XML 1.0 document encoded in UTF-8, with the MIME type message/imdn+xml and the namespace urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:imdn. The root element is <imdn>. Its children are:

  • <message-id> (mandatory): the Message-ID of the original message.
  • <datetime> (mandatory): when the original message was sent, not when the IMDN was made.
  • <recipient-uri> and <original-recipient-uri> (optional): the final and original recipient. The second MUST be present if the message carried Original-To.
  • <subject> (optional): the text and language of the Subject field, for human matching.
  • One of <delivery-notification>, <processing-notification> or <display-notification>, each containing a <status>.

The RFC includes a RelaxNG schema with extension points so later specifications can add elements. A receiver tells which kind of message it holds by looking at the content: it is a delivery notification when the type is message/imdn+xml, the disposition is notification and a <delivery-notification> element is present, and likewise for the other two kinds.
sections.eli5: A receipt is a small form with boxes: which letter, when it was sent, who got it, and a tick for what happened to it.

sections.title: Carrying IMDNs over SIP and MSRP
sections.content:
Over SIP, both messages and IMDNs travel in MESSAGE requests whose Content-type is message/cpim. A recipient that has sent a 2xx response MAY then send a positive-delivery or display notification once the message has really reached the user or application, and SHOULD send a negative-delivery notification if it learns the final recipient never got it. It MUST NOT send a negative-delivery notification after a non-2xx final response. IMDNs are addressed to the address in the original SIP From field.

SIP proxies MUST NOT generate IMDNs but forward them like any other request. An intermediary must not claim delivery just because it received a 2xx from downstream, since that does not mean the message reached its final destination. Anonymous senders SHOULD NOT request notifications because there is no return address.

For MSRP (RFC 4975), the RFC does not define IMDN transport. MSRP already has its own positive and negative delivery reports, and display or processing notices matter less in session mode because the recipient normally renders messages immediately.
sections.eli5: The receipts ride along in the same mail truck as the messages. The trucks in the middle just pass them on without writing their own.

sections.title: Security and Privacy
sections.content:
IMDNs give a fine-grained view of what a recipient is doing, so the RFC asks for careful confidentiality protection. Listed threats include flooding a target with IMDNs, forging or modifying IMDNs, learning hidden addresses behind an intermediary, eavesdropping, and denial of service through large list expansion. The protocol cannot defend against a recipient who lies about the time, against deletion of an IMDN in transit, or against an intermediary that reveals a downstream identity.

The integrity rules are cumulative. If the recipient has a certificate, it MUST sign the IMDN. If the original message was encrypted, the recipient or intermediary MUST encrypt the IMDN body. The same level of security applied to a message MUST be applied to its IMDNs. Because routing information sits in the application-layer payload, the design rules out end-to-end encryption.

On privacy, a recipient may silently ignore an IMDN request, and obtaining the user's consent before sending one is strongly RECOMMENDED. Systems required by regulation, such as in health care or finance, may send IMDNs without asking. The RFC also states that IMDNs cannot be relied on as a certified delivery service: they can be forged or lost, and a recipient can bypass them by policy.

A display notification means the message was shown, not that a person read it.
sections.eli5: A receipt tells on what you did, so it should be kept private and signed so it cannot be faked. You are also allowed to say "no thanks" and not send one.
